prompt.brief: Design a log-anomaly platform that normalizes heterogeneous logs, extracts templates, detects novel patterns, clusters related errors, correlates them with system events, and alerts operators with evidence.
successSignals: Keep raw logs immutable and derive normalized events, templates, embeddings, baselines, anomalies, correlations, and alert state.
Use streaming template extraction and windowed baselines while controlling cardinality, retention cost, and false positives.
Combine deterministic rules with statistical or ML detectors, attach representative log evidence, and support feedback loops.
Explain late logs, schema drift, model cold start, alert deduplication, privacy, tenant isolation, and replay.

functional: Collect logs, parse formats, extract templates and fields, index normalized events, and calculate anomaly scores by service and window.
Search by text or semantic similarity, show correlated deployments and metrics, group alerts, and provide representative evidence.
Support detector configuration, feedback, suppression windows, retention, PII redaction, replay, and incident export.
nonFunctional: Process 1 million log lines per second with bounded agent overhead and detect high-confidence anomalies within one window.
Scale search and detection by tenant, service, time, and template while isolating noisy services and high-cardinality fields.
Make ingestion and alert delivery deduplicable; retain raw evidence so a detector can be replayed after a model change.
Continue ingestion and rule-based detection when embeddings, model workers, or search indexes are degraded.
scaleAssumptions: Ingest 1 million lines per second from 10,000 services and retain searchable recent data plus archived raw logs.
Partition by tenant, service, event time, and template; isolate bursty incidents and high-cardinality labels.
Retain redacted raw events, parser versions, detector models, anomaly evidence, and alert decisions for replay.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Log-anomaly platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Log-anomaly platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Log-anomaly platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Log-anomaly platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Log-anomaly platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Log-anomaly platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Log-anomaly platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Log-anomaly platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Log-anomaly platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
